column2: My owl has taken her last breath. They say owls are Verena's own birds, sent to keep watch where the goddess cannot. I thought I was her keeper all these years. Now that it is time to send her off, I wonder if she was not keeping watch over me.
My owl won't wake up. They tell me she has flown on to the next world, but why would she go without telling me?
I shall light a pyre in her name.
You hold a ceremony far grander than most would expect for a bird.\n
She was family, and shall lie beside my ancestors.
Her name is cut into a stone, for generations to remember.\n
No matter. I have already taken in her soul. Hooo HOOOOO!
You seek out the highest balcony in [Root.Location.GetName] for a midnight flight.\n§Y20%§! chance: §Y[Root.GetTitledFirstName]§! dies!\n
Birds are mean.
You wish you had a dog.\n
A servant gasps as I throw myself from the balcony. Wind in my hair, I soar through the night and it seems to go on forever. The landing is soft: I am in a hay cart! A pigeon eyes me with suspicion.
A servant gasps as I step off the balcony. The fool does not know I can fly! The air caresses my cheek as the wind carries me on, faster and faster!
That cannot have been the highest tower in [Root.Location.GetName].
With barely a sprained ankle, you survive!\n
I always knew I could fl-
You fall to your death.\n
My cat curled up in its favourite spot by the window last night. I think it knew it did not have long left in this world. At least it went peacefully.\n
They tell me my cat has gone to live with one of my distant aunts. She has a fine house in the country, and my cat will be very happy there, roaming the woods and playing with lots of other cats.
It shall be buried in the garden, where it loved to play.
Whenever you stroll past the rose bushes, you will remember your cat.\n
The whole court shall celebrate the adventurous life of my cat!
Your cat would be honoured.\n
That cat was possessed, always giving me the evil eye!
You order the remains of the cat burned at the stake!\n
I'm glad it's in a better place!
You never see your cat again.\n

The guard nods and walks off, sullen. "Don't argue!" I shout after him as he disappears down the corridor.\nNow that I think about it, I never smelled any smoke, and later I find a small grave behind the stables!
He wouldn't... Everyone knows you cannot simply bury a cursed creature.
How odd!

For some time I have suspected that [cat_hater.GetFirstName] has less than warm feelings for my cat. Today I was proven right, when [cat_hater.GetSheHe] threw a fit because the cat drank from [cat_hater.GetHerHis] cup! [cat_hater.GetSheHeCap] demands that I get rid of the animal.
I will get rid of the animal, if that is your wish.
I am sure someone can take care of the cat.
Never will I be parted from my precious kitty!
Perhaps I should get rid of YOU?
Show §Y[cat_hater.GetTitledFirstName]§! what you think of people who hate cats!\n
Let me introduce you to my other kitties...

Things have been tense between [cat_hater.GetFirstName] and me since that tantrum the other day. [cat_hater.GetSheHeCap] has grown more and more irritable, and today it came to a harsh ultimatum: I must choose between [cat_hater.GetHerHim] and the cat.
I will get rid of the creature, since you feel so strongly about it.
You get rid of the cat to please §Y[cat_hater.GetTitledFirstName]§!.\n
The choice is simple. Kitty would never put me in this position!
You choose your beloved companion over the tiresome §Y[cat_hater.GetTitledFirstName]§!.\n

Today I went to visit my old cat at [From.GetTitledFirstName]'s home. I found [From.GetHerHim] playing with the little furball with great enthusiasm, and watched them for several minutes before I made myself known.
Today I went to visit my old hound at [From.GetTitledFirstName]'s home. I found them playing together with great enthusiasm, and watched them for several minutes before I made myself known.
Thank you, [From.GetFirstName], for taking such good care of my cat!
Thank you, [From.GetFirstName], for taking such good care of my hound!
You and §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! bond over your love of cats.\n
You and §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! bond over your love of dogs.\n

Today I went to visit my old cat at [From.GetTitledFirstName]'s home. But [From.GetSheHe] could not produce it, and when I angrily demanded the truth, [From.GetSheHe] admitted to getting rid of the cat a few days ago.

Today I went to visit my old hound at [From.GetTitledFirstName]'s home. But [From.GetSheHe] could not produce it, and when I angrily demanded the truth, [From.GetSheHe] admitted to getting rid of the dog a few days ago.
What have you done, you [GetRootFromInsult]?!
You tell §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! exactly what you think of [From.GetHerHis] behaviour.\n

When it is asleep or curled in my lap, my cat is a little angel. I do not understand how something can be so calm one moment and fly across the room the next. When these fits take it, it climbs over all my belongings, and it is only luck when nothing breaks.
It's just playing! If something breaks, I can easily replace it.
Let the cat do whatever it pleases.\n
Come here, kitty! No, no, not that one!
Chase the cat and stop it from ruining anything.\n
Blasted beast! Leave one scratch and I'll wring your neck!
Punish the cat if it breaks anything.\n
The cat leaves you and finds a new home.\n

[rabbit_parent.GetTitledFirstName] storms into my hall. My beloved cat, [rabbit_parent.GetSheHe] claims, has killed [rabbit_parent.GetHerHis] [rabbit_child.GetSonDaughter]'s pet rabbit, and now [rabbit_parent.GetSheHe] demands some kind of compensation.
Calm down, [rabbit_parent.GetFirstName]. I will buy [rabbit_child.GetFirstName] a new pet.
Replace §Y[rabbit_child.GetTitledFirstName]'s§! dead rabbit to please [rabbit_child.GetHerHis] [rabbit_parent.GetFatherMother].\n
I am most sorry. My companion will not be a threat any longer.
Put down your pet before it can hurt anyone else.\n
Impossible. My angel would never hurt a fly!
Refuse to believe §Y[rabbit_parent.GetTitledFirstName]§!.\n

I sit by the fire with my precious cat curled in my lap, stroking it slowly as I stare into the flames. My furry friend has a good life here with me. But what about all the other cats who have no home? The ones no one feeds, or combs, or cuddles? Perhaps I could take care of them!
I just want to hug all of them!
Adopt more cats. There is plenty of room in the keep!\n
But I can't, because that would be mad...
One is enough. Still, you cannot stop thinking about the cats, and how sweet they are...\n
Your cat always seems to know when you need comfort. It appears out of nowhere, jumps into your lap and purrs softly as you stroke it.
What greater gift than the love of a cat?

Your two pets truly fight like cat and dog. You can barely sleep unless you lock them in separate rooms, and the cat has taken to hiding at bedtime for fear of being shut away. Yesterday you spent the better part of an hour looking for it. You cannot stand this much longer...
They will sort it out in time.
You give your cat and your hound the chance to get used to each other.\n
I will find a new master for my hound.
The cat is clearly unhappy. I will find it a new home.
Today, as you set out to hunt, your loyal hound was nowhere to be found. As you called its name, the stable master told you he had seen a cat chase a dog across the courtyard. Now it is gone...

It is time for bed and you are searching for your cat. You try your latest trick, luring it out with scraps from the kitchen, but for the first time it does not work. After an hour you give up and call for your hound. It comes running with a limp little body in its jaws...
Time was all your pets needed. One day they simply stopped fighting, and since then they have been the best of friends. You often find them playing or dozing together. They seem much happier.
The fault is mine. The cat is just an animal...
My hound is never coming back and it is all your fault, evil beast!
Get rid of your cat.\n
The fault is mine. The hound is just an animal...
How... how could you! Bad dog! BAD DOG!
Get rid of your hound.\n
How sweet! I knew they would get along in the end.

[pet_accuser.GetTitledFirstName] has been watching my cat for weeks. Today, before half the court, [pet_accuser.GetSheHe] named it a witch's familiar: a thing that creeps through the halls at night and carries whispers to some hag in the woods, or worse, to the Dark Gods. Witch hunters have burned whole villages on less, [pet_accuser.GetSheHe] reminds me, and [pet_accuser.GetSheHe] wants the beast on a pyre by sundown. The cat yawns.
Burn it, then. Better a dead cat than a damned house.
The cat goes to the pyre. The court approves, mostly.\n
It is a cat. It catches mice, not souls.
A familiar? Perhaps. Would you like to meet its master?
The candles gutter as you speak, and §Y[pet_accuser.GetTitledFirstName]§! goes pale. [pet_accuser.GetSheHeCap] will not forget it.\n
The pyre is lit. It would be a shame to waste it.
§Y[pet_accuser.GetTitledFirstName]§! burns instead of the cat. Killing a hunter of witches will not sit well with the faithful.\n

A scruffy cat with one torn ear has slipped past the guards and into the hall. It ignores the courtiers, the hounds and the steward's broom, walks straight up to the high seat, and climbs into your lap as if it had always lived there. It looks up at you and waits.
Stroke the kitty.
You may stay, little one.
Kick the filthy thing off!
